Question
========
Which I/O technique allows the process to continue execution while the I/O is still being performed?


Answerlist
----------
* Blocking I/O
* Non-blocking I/O
* Async I/O
* Buffered I/O

Solution
========
With asynchronous I/O the process submits the operation and immediately goes on doing useful work; the completion is signalled later. Non-blocking I/O only avoids sleeping: it returns immediately telling you that nothing is ready yet, and you have to come back and ask again.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. The process is put to sleep until the operation completes.
* 0. It returns immediately without performing the operation, so you must poll again.
* 1. The operation is started in the background and the process is notified on completion.
* 0. Buffering reduces the number of calls but does not by itself overlap I/O with computation.
